missions.name: Controlled construction and HVAC delivery
missions.objective: Convert project requirements into qualified field teams, controlled work packages, inspection evidence, nonconformance closure, commissioning, and authorized owner acceptance.
missions.why: Construction readiness depends on more than a schedule: the correct licensed, trained, supervised, and independent quality personnel must be available at each control phase with usable evidence.

roles.title: Project manager
roles.responsibility: Own scope, schedule, staffing coordination, client decisions, and escalation of project gaps.

roles.title: Quality control manager
roles.responsibility: Plan and govern preparatory, initial, follow-up, inspection, test, nonconformance, and acceptance controls independently from production pressure.

roles.title: Trade foreman
roles.responsibility: Lead the assigned trade crew, confirm daily readiness, execute the approved work method, and provide completion evidence.

roles.title: Commissioning and acceptance authority
roles.responsibility: Verify system performance and independently accept, conditionally accept, reject, or require correction.

controls.title: Qualified trade coverage
controls.description: Require current role-specific licensing, certification, training, availability, and backup coverage before a controlled work package is Ready.

controls.title: Three-phase quality control
controls.description: Require preparatory, initial, and follow-up controls with assigned performers, verifiers, criteria, evidence, and release authority.

controls.title: Commissioning and work acceptance
controls.description: Prevent closure until tests, nonconformances, completion items, turnover records, and authorized acceptance are complete.

expectedShortfalls: A licensed or certified trade role may be unavailable for the required work window.
The project may lack independent quality or commissioning coverage.
A critical control point may have incomplete or expired evidence.
resultingGaps: Work may proceed without qualified supervision or required inspection.
Defects, rework, safety exposure, or schedule delay may increase.
The owner cannot confidently accept or operate the completed system.
prohibitedAutomation: No agent may represent itself as a licensed contractor, engineer, inspector, safety authority, or owner acceptance authority.
No work package may be accepted from photos, sensor output, or an AI summary alone.

missions.name: Governed local and state building permit operations
missions.objective: Identify the correct authorities having jurisdiction, determine permit requirements, prepare current official forms and attachment packages, route signatures and professional certifications, submit only when authorized, process comments, coordinate inspections, and register official closeout evidence.
missions.why: Construction and HVAC work can be delayed, stopped, rejected, or exposed to legal and financial risk when the wrong jurisdiction, outdated forms, missing licenses, incomplete plans, unsupported attestations, unpaid fees, unresolved comments, or missing inspections are not detected before work begins.
sourceRecords: official jurisdiction and building department source
adopted code edition and local amendment

roles.title: Permit coordinator
roles.responsibility: Coordinate jurisdiction research, form versioning, permit matrices, application preparation, attachment control, submission readiness, comments, inspections, and closeout evidence.

roles.title: Licensed contractor
roles.responsibility: Verify contractor scope, provide required contractor information and attestations, review the application package, and authorize contractor-controlled submissions where permitted.

roles.title: Responsible design professional
roles.responsibility: Provide and approve professional calculations, drawings, certifications, responses, signatures, and seals within the professional's lawful scope.

roles.title: Authorized permit submitter
roles.responsibility: Perform or explicitly authorize the irreversible submission through the official portal, email, or manual channel after all readiness gates pass.

roles.title: Permit fee financial approver
roles.responsibility: Verify budget availability and approve permit, plan-review, inspection, reinspection, utility, and related fees without delegating payment release to the permit agent.

controls.title: Verified jurisdiction and current form
controls.description: Require official sources, verified authority having jurisdiction, current code edition, local amendments, current official form, retrieval timestamp, and checksum before an application may be prepared for submission.

controls.title: Permit application package completeness
controls.description: Require complete and verified fields, plans, calculations, energy forms, product approvals, owner authorization, licenses, insurance, signatures, seals, and other jurisdiction-specific attachments.

controls.title: Human submission authorization
controls.description: Prevent irreversible portal, email, or manual submission until the authorized applicant or submitter confirms the final package and all attestations.

controls.title: Professional judgment boundary
controls.description: Route design changes, code interpretations, calculations, certifications, signatures, seals, and professional review comments to the responsible licensed professional.

controls.title: Permit fee financial control
controls.description: Require an approved budget decision before fees are paid or a fee-required submission is recorded.

controls.title: Official inspection and certificate closeout
controls.description: Prevent permit closeout from supporting project acceptance until official inspections, correction closure, commissioning records, and issued permit or certificate evidence are registered.

expectedShortfalls: The project address or parcel may map to the wrong permitting authority.
The application form or portal requirements may be outdated or unverified.
Required contractor licenses, professional credentials, signatures, seals, plans, calculations, or attachments may be missing.
Permit fees may not have an approved budget or payment authority.
Review comments may lack a responsible professional or response deadline.
The work package may not be ready for a requested inspection.
resultingGaps: The permit application may be rejected, delayed, or submitted to the wrong authority.
Construction may begin without lawful authorization or may be subject to a stop-work order.
Professional, contractor, owner, or financial liability may be created by unsupported attestations.
Failed inspections and unresolved comments may delay commissioning, occupancy, payment, and owner acceptance.
prohibitedAutomation: No agent may sign or fabricate an owner, contractor, or professional attestation.
No agent may create or apply an architect or engineer seal.
No agent may claim to approve, issue, inspect, certify, or close a permit on behalf of a governmental authority.
No agent may bypass CAPTCHA, anti-bot, payment, signature, or irreversible portal controls.
No agent may state that a permit is not required without official authority confirmation.
No permit fee may be paid without separate FinOps approval and authorized external payment execution.
kpis: permit and certificate closeout cycle time

marketingProof.proofStatement: Demonstrate a traceable chain from project requirement through permit jurisdiction, current official forms, qualified workforce, application package, authorized submission, quality controls, inspections, commissioning evidence, permit closeout, and owner acceptance.
baselineEvidence: sample quality plan and inspection records
sample permit matrix and application checklist
baseline permit comment and inspection cycle
targetEvidence: verified jurisdiction and official permit form versions
official synthetic inspection and certificate evidence
proofGates: Use synthetic project and permit data until data-classification, portal, customer, and authority approvals are complete.
Construction authority, permit authority, license, professional credential, signature, and seal evidence must be independently verified.
A production permit case study requires an actual authorized project, official submission receipt, issued permit, official inspections, closeout certificate, and project-owner approval.
Outcome claims require an approved baseline and project-owner acceptance.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim OSHA, code, permit, LEED, contract, or licensing compliance from software use alone.
Do not claim that TaskStaff approves permits or replaces licensed professionals or building officials.
Do not claim faster permit issuance, reduced defects, lower cost, or shorter schedule without outcome-verified project records.

implementation.nextAction: Run a synthetic commercial HVAC replacement scenario through jurisdiction resolution, permit matrix, official form registration, application preparation, signatures and seals, fee approval, authorized submission, comments, inspections, commissioning, certificate closeout, and owner acceptance.
